XI.}}</noinclude>she vvas come vvhere {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas, seeing him, fel at his feete, and saith to him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=33}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore vvhen he savv her vveeping, and the Ievves that vvere come vvith her, vveeping, he groned in spirit, and troubled him self, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=34}}† and said, VVhere haue you laid him? They say to him, Lord, come and see. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=35}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} vvept. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=36}}† The Ievves therfore said, Behold hovv he loued him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=37}}† But certaine of them said, Could not he that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 9, 6.''}}* opened the eies of the blinde man, make that this man should not die? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=38}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore againe groning in him self, commeth to the graue. and it vvas a caue: and a stone vvas laid ouer it. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=39}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith, Take avvay the stone. Martha the sister of him that vvas dead, saith to him, Lord, novv he stinketh, for he is novv of foure daies. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=40}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to her, Did not I say to thee, that if thou beleeue, thou shalt see the glorie of God? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=41}}† They tooke therfore the stone avvay. And {{sc|Iesvs}} lifting his eies vpvvard, said, Father, I giue thee thankes that thou hast heard me. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=42}}† and I did know that thou doest alvvaies heare me, but for the people that standeth about, haue I said it, that they may beleeue that thou hast sent me. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=43}}† VVhen he had said these things, he cried vvith a loude voice, Lazarus, come forth. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=44}}† And forthvvith he came forth that had been dead, bound feete and handes vvith vvinding bandes, and his face vvas tied vvith a napkin. {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Cyril ''li. 7 c. vlt. in Io''. and S. August. ''Tract. 49 in Io''. apply this to the Apostles and Priests authoritie of absoluing sinners: affirming Christ to reuiue none from sinne, but in the Church and by the Priests ministerie.}}∷ Loose him, and let him goe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=45}}† Many therfore of the Ievves that vvere come to Marie and Martha, and had seen the things that {{sc|Iesvs}} did, beleeued in him.⊣ {{verse|chapter=11|verse=46}}† And certaine of them vvent to the Pharisees, and told them the things that {{sc|Iesvs}} did. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=47}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō friday in Passion weeke.}}The cheefe priests therfore and the pharisees gathered a councel, and said, VVhat doe vve, for this man doeth many signes. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=48}}† If vve let him alone so, al vvil beleeue in him: and the Romanes vvil come, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Al men, but specially Nations must take heede, that whiles to saue their temporal state, they forsake God: they lose not both as the Iewes did. ''Aug. tract. 49 in Io''.}}∷ take avvay our place and nation. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=49}}† But one of them named Caiphas, being the high priest of that yere, said to them, You knovv nothing, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=50}}† neither doe you consider that it is expedient for vs that one man die for the people, and the vvhole nation perish not. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=51}}† And this he said not of him self: but {{sup|‖}} being the high priest of that yere, he prophecied that {{sc|Iesvs}} should die for the nation: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=52}}† and not only for the nation, but to gather into one the children of God that vvere dispersed. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=53}}† From that day therfore they deuised to kil him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=54}}† {{sc|Iesvs}}<noinclude>{{rh|||therfore}}</noinclude>
